title: Operator escrow and live-rotation proof plan for private deploys
creator: Lea Chen
description: Goal: Produce an operator-escrow and live-key-rotation proof plan that satisfies enterprise customers' audit requirements for Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). This ticket defines acceptance criteria, required artifacts, and a concrete sign-off checklist covering SSO/SAML behavior, RBAC least-privilege mappings, HSM/KMS rotation evidence, audit-log fidelity, and emergency operator escrow processes. The PRD addendum will be attached and used as the canonical checklist during rollout to customers and during SOC-style audits.
acceptance_criteria: SSO/SAML: A reproducible test matrix demonstrating SAML assertion lifecycle (init, renew, replay protection) across three IdPs with logs retained for 365 days.
RBAC: A least-privilege role mapping doc plus automated policy tests (CI) proving no privilege escalation path in the operator role set.

KMS/HSM: Evidence of key wrapping/unwrapping with customer-managed keys (CMK) including test vectors showing successful live-rotation with zero data-loss and a documented fallback that preserves decryption ability for in-flight tokens.
HSM Quorum: Test results from a 3-node HSM quorum simulation demonstrating rotation, partial-node failure, and recovery procedures with step-by-step logs attached.
Audit logs: End-to-end audit trail for admin/operator actions (key creation, rotation, role grants, SAML config changes) with immutable storage proof (hash snapshot) and retention rules implemented.
Operator escrow: Signed escrow procedure and encrypted escrow artifact delivered to customer-admin with access procedure validated by two independent operators and an auditable approval flow.

Rollback & emergency access: A validated runbook showing how to revoke a compromised operator key, accelerate rotation, and execute emergency-escrow retrieval without violating least-privilege constraints.
Automated verification: CI job(s) that run the above checks in a staging environment and produce a human-readable evidence bundle for auditors.
Stakeholder sign-off: Security, Product, and two Customer Success engineers have signed acceptance in Confluence.
Documentation: Console UX changes documented with screenshots, and an operations runbook published under private-ops/escrow-playbook (Confluence).
signoff_checklist: [ ] SAML test matrix executed for IdP-A, IdP-B, IdP-C with logs exported
[ ] RBAC policy lint and attack-surface report attached (no critical findings)
[ ] KMS rotation test (live) executed and recorded: evidence bundle (rotation-2025-02-27.tar.gz)
[ ] HSM quorum failover test report attached with node traces
[ ] Audit snapshot created and hash published to immutable storage (sha256 hash included)
[ ] Operator escrow artifact encrypted and escrow-release policy documented
[ ] Emergency access drill completed and signed by two operators (recording link)
[ ] CI verification pipeline green (job ids attached)
[ ] Security review completed and approval provided in this ticket comments
notes: Trade-offs: Full HSM replication across customer regions is out of scope for this cycle due to cost; instead we provide a documented fallback that relies on wrapped CMKs and a signed escrow artifact.

Decision: Use envelope encryption with KMS for data-at-rest and maintain minimal operator key material in HSM; rotation will be orchestrated by the operator service with a 4-step handshake to avoid split-brain.

Open question: whether to surface an 'admin-override' button in the Console for escrow retrieval. UX prefers manual request flow to avoid accidental release; Security prefers an auditable, time-locked automatic release. Action: prototyping and threat assessment in ENG-57812.
Backward compatibility: Releases must support decryption of tokens issued with keys within the last 90 days. Acceptance tests include tokens issued at t-100 days to confirm documented fallback works.
